title: A six-neuron counterexample to the target-free clique conjecture
summary: The target-free clique conjecture asserts that the supports of stable fixed points of a nondegenerate combinatorial threshold-linear network (CTLN) are exactly its target-free cliques: bidirected cliques for which no outside vertex receives an edge from every clique vertex. We give an explicit six-neuron counterexample. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the CTLN defined by one fixed graph at $δ=29\varepsilon/25$ is nondegenerate and has a stable fixed point with nonclique full support.
